name: Arrival & details
note: Before guests arrive. Capture the room while it is still untouched.

shots.title: Venue establishing wide
shots.cue: Show where the day takes place. Hold a clean wide; coordinate with Luke if a drone is needed.

editor.description: Opening establishing wide. It introduces the place before vows begin.

shots.title: Empty ceremony space
shots.cue: Frame the arch, aisle and chairs. Capture a steady wide plus a closer detail.

editor.description: Opening ceremony-space detail. This follows the establishing shot before the rings.

shots.title: Rings & invitation
shots.cue: Find soft light. Keep the rings and lettering sharp; make one slow, deliberate move.

editor.description: Opening rings or invitation detail. This closes the detail introduction before preparation.

shots.title: Dress detail
shots.cue: Frame the whole dress, then its texture. Keep the background clean and leave time at each end.

editor.description: Opening detail fallback. Use the dress here when rings or invitations are unavailable.

shots.title: Reception details
shots.cue: Capture tables, flowers and personal touches before the room fills.

editor.description: Second or third opening picture. Reception tables, flowers and room details can introduce the wedding alongside the ceremony detail or rings.

name: Getting ready
note: Small actions and real relationships give the film its personal moments.

shots.title: Bride preparation
shots.cue: Capture an action, such as makeup or fastening the dress. Watch for the face and hands.

editor.description: Bride preparation under the groom’s vows. Hold a complete action, then move to groom preparation.

shots.title: Groom preparation
shots.cue: Capture the tie, jacket or boutonniere. Hold the action long enough for it to finish.

editor.description: Groom preparation under the groom’s vows. One developed action supports this longer preparation slot.

shots.title: Bride & parent moment
shots.cue: If a parent first look is planned, be ready before it starts. Stay through the expression and hug.

editor.description: Bride-vow picture alternatives. A parent reaction or hug belongs here when her words make that relationship relevant.

shots.title: Candid bride reaction
shots.cue: Look for laughter and conversation during preparation. Let the moment develop naturally.

editor.description: Preparation or bride-vow picture alternatives. Use a distinct reaction; avoid repeating a scene already used.

name: First look & portraits
note: If scheduled before the ceremony. Let Luke lead positioning and keep a complementary angle.

shots.title: First look reaction
shots.cue: When scheduled, be ready before the reveal and record the full approach, turn and reaction. Coordinate angles with Luke and keep rolling.

editor.description: Optional first-look picture during either partner’s vows. Let the emotion and available musical space determine its place.

shots.title: Hands & partial reveal
shots.cue: Start with hands or a small detail of the couple. Keep the movement gentle and purposeful.

editor.description: Early portrait reveal during vows. Hands and partial views lead into portraits with faces visible.

shots.title: Couple walking
shots.cue: Capture them walking together during portraits, with both faces visible. Leave room in their direction of travel.

editor.description: Portrait progression during vows. Walking develops the reveal into visible faces and connection.

shots.title: Extra portrait angle
shots.cue: After the first look or main portrait setup is covered, gather a complementary angle of the couple together. Hold their connection and leave generous handles.

editor.description: Additional portrait coverage under vows. A complementary angle gives the editor an alternative after the main reveal or portrait.

name: Ceremony
note: Record every scheduled ceremony moment, including readings, vows, ring exchange and special rituals. Keep uninterrupted coverage from your assigned angle and coordinate any changes with Luke before the processional.

shots.title: Guests & family
shots.cue: Capture attentive faces before the ceremony. Find parents and close family in advance.

editor.description: Ceremony anticipation or a meaningful vow-line cutaway. Keep the couple on screen by default unless the words lead naturally to someone else.

shots.title: Aisle walk
shots.cue: Record the full processional from the assigned angle. Hold the bride’s approach through her arrival without stopping or reframing abruptly.

editor.description: Aisle walk under the bride’s vows. Let her approach develop into ceremony anticipation; the handoff has its own coverage card.

shots.title: Groom reaction shot
shots.cue: Be on the groom before he sees her. Stay on his reaction instead of chasing the aisle camera.

editor.description: Groom reaction during the bride’s aisle walk. Preserve his authentic expression as the ceremony anticipation builds.

shots.title: Bride handoff
shots.cue: Hold the parent’s final hug, the handoff to the groom and the transition to the altar. Start before the bride arrives and keep recording through the entire exchange.

editor.description: The handoff follows the aisle walk in ceremony anticipation. Preserve the complete exchange for the documentary edit.

shots.title: Vows & listening reaction
shots.cue: Hold a stable second angle on the speaker and listener. Keep expressions visible and avoid repositioning mid-vow.

editor.description: On-camera groom vow hold and reaction/handoff. If he is still speaking, hold on him before the next voice enters.

shots.title: Ring exchange detail
shots.cue: Record the full ring exchange from your assigned angle. Keep the hands and rings visible where possible without crossing Cam A, and hold through the finished action.

editor.description: Required ceremony coverage. Record the entire exchange cleanly; an excerpt can support the ceremony picture even when it has no fixed highlight slot.

shots.title: Pronouncement, kiss & cheer
shots.cue: Be ready before the invitation to kiss. Hold through the kiss and the full natural cheer.

editor.description: Pronouncement, kiss and full natural cheer. Preserve the officiant’s invitation and let the cheer finish before reception music takes over.

shots.title: Recessional
shots.cue: Keep rolling as the couple turns and walks back down the aisle. Capture the complete walk, cheers and any pause or kiss without interrupting the take.

editor.description: Required ceremony event coverage after the kiss and cheer. Preserve the full exit before moving to reception coverage.

name: Golden-hour portraits
note: Gather plenty of varied portraits for both partners’ vow sequences: wide, medium, close, details and movement. Hold each action with generous handles, then change angle or composition. Follow the actual sunset window.

shots.title: Faces, embrace & kiss
shots.cue: Use the warm light for a close portrait. Let the couple hold, laugh and kiss without rushing.

editor.description: Portrait progression during vows. Holding and kissing complete the reveal; use different pictures for each partner.

shots.title: Closing wide
shots.cue: Capture the couple within the landscape. Hold a clean ending; coordinate a walking-away or drone version with Luke.

editor.description: Final closing wide. The couple walks away as the music settles, visually echoing the opening.

shots.title: Playful couple moment
shots.cue: Let the couple laugh, turn or move together. Capture the natural payoff without rushing them.

editor.description: Alternative portrait picture during vows. Use a playful moment where the words and mood support it, with different pictures for each partner.

shots.title: Couple in the landscape
shots.cue: Capture a wide showing the couple within the setting. Hold long enough for a clean edit, then change composition or distance.

editor.description: A scenic portrait establishes the couple within the location under vows. Gather separate compositions for each partner’s vow sequence.

shots.title: Medium portrait & connection
shots.cue: Frame both faces clearly from the waist or chest up. Hold eye contact, closeness and small natural movements.

editor.description: A medium portrait bridges the wide reveal and closer emotional pictures. Keep several distinct holds available under both sets of vows.

shots.title: Close faces & expressions
shots.cue: Get a clean close portrait of their faces and expressions. Collect several quiet holds, smiles and reactions without cutting them short.

editor.description: Close expressions carry the intimate vow-led picture. Leave generous handles and collect distinct pictures for each partner.

shots.title: Walking together in warm light
shots.cue: Capture a full walking action together: toward camera, across frame or away. Keep faces visible for at least one angle and leave room to move.

editor.description: Walking provides movement under vows; a wide walking-away version can also close the film. Gather different directions and distances.

shots.title: Hands & small portrait details
shots.cue: Gather linked hands, rings and small gestures while the couple is together. Hold each detail steadily and capture the action finishing.

editor.description: A partial reveal begins the portrait progression before visible faces and connection. These details give the editor variety under vows.

shots.title: Twirl & flowing dress
shots.cue: When it suits the couple, capture the complete turn and their reaction. Give the dress room and leave handles before and after.

editor.description: A complete twirl offers a lively portrait alternative where the vow mood and music support movement.

shots.title: Dip & playful kiss
shots.cue: If Luke directs a dip or playful kiss, capture the whole action and the laugh afterward. Choose a complementary angle.

editor.description: A playful portrait alternative. The lead-in and payoff let the editor choose a complete action instead of cutting into its middle.

shots.title: Backlight & silhouette
shots.cue: Try a backlit or silhouette composition after getting clean faces. Hold a simple shape with the couple clearly separated from the background.

editor.description: An atmospheric portrait alternative under vows, or a quiet wide ending when the song and setting support it.

shots.title: Veil & fabric movement
shots.cue: If there is a veil, let fabric and light create gentle movement around the couple. Keep their connection visible and the take steady.

editor.description: A soft portrait alternative adds visual texture without losing the couple during the vow-led picture.

name: Reception & dancing
note: Every event on the schedule is essential when it happens. Confirm the running order with Luke and the coordinator; cover additional games, traditions or performances with the same uninterrupted event standard.

shots.title: Other scheduled reception events
shots.cue: Follow the running order for entrances, garter tosses, games, traditions and performances. Every scheduled event is essential: set your angle before it starts and record the whole moment through the final reaction.

editor.description: Required coverage of every additional scheduled event. The examples show an entrance, a garter toss and cake cutting; retain each complete event for the documentary edit and choose a fitting highlight excerpt.

shots.title: Reception speeches
shots.cue: Cover every speaker from before the introduction through the final applause. Confirm clean audio and your assigned speaker or reaction angle with Luke; never stop mid-speech.

editor.description: Required speech coverage. Keep the full speech and matching reaction angle for the documentary edit; a meaningful excerpt can enter the highlight.

shots.title: Speech reactions
shots.cue: Coordinate with Luke: cover the couple continuously while the speaker talks. Keep rolling through every speech, laughter, tears and applause.

editor.description: Continuous reaction angle paired with the speech camera in the documentary edit. Select a meaningful laugh or emotional beat for the reception montage.

shots.title: Cake cutting
shots.cue: Record the full cutting, feeding and reactions. Keep hands, cake and faces in the frame and continue through the finish.

editor.description: Required reception event coverage. The complete action serves the documentary edit; cutting or feeding can fit the reception montage.

shots.title: First dance
shots.cue: Keep a stable second angle with both faces visible when possible. Stay through turns and the ending.

editor.description: Reception movement. Dancing provides a clear action for the faster reception picture rhythm.

shots.title: Parent dance
shots.cue: Record every scheduled parent dance from start to finish. Hold a clean second angle with faces visible; stay through the final embrace.

editor.description: Required reception event coverage. The full dance supports the documentary edit; an emotional excerpt can fit the reception montage.

shots.title: Flower toss
shots.cue: Be ready before the countdown. Frame the throw and catching group; record continuously through the catch and celebration.

editor.description: Required reception event coverage. Preserve setup, throw, catch and reactions for the full edit; choose the payoff for the highlight.

shots.title: Open dancing
shots.cue: After securing the scheduled events, capture joyful faces and complete dance moves. Mix wider groups with close moments; keep flower toss coverage separate.

editor.description: Energetic reception picture. Use varied faces and completed actions as cuts become more frequent.

shots.title: Extra dance-floor angles
shots.cue: Gather additional guest moments and views of the party. Mix wider groups with closer faces, and let a complete dance action unfold.

editor.description: An extra reception angle provides scale and energy between closer dance moments. Secure all scheduled events first.

shots.title: Send-off & exit
shots.cue: When scheduled, check the route and exposure before it begins. Keep recording the full exit, kiss or final pause and the celebration afterward.

editor.description: Required exit coverage. A final departure may close the reception story or support the ending, depending on the approved film structure.
